rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts, retaliation)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not end a tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause, and must give a written statement of cause. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay relocation assistance of 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors or disabled tenants) or waive that rent, give 30/60 days' notice, and offer re-rental if the unit is re-offered within 5 years. Buyout agreements are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior/disabled) for no-fault terminations
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.effective_date_note: Division as retitled/expanded by O-21647 N.S. effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, dormitories, shared-facility rentals with live-in landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence, owner-occupied duplex, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years, and separately alienable property (e.g. condos/single-family) whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and tenants were given written notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief and damages including punitive; wrongful eviction damages of at least 3x actual economic damages; at least 3x relocation assistance owed; attorney's fees; notices void for noncompliance; City enforcement with civil and criminal remedies.
rules.interaction: Rights are in addition to state and federal rights; consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but provides greater relocation assistance.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property owned by non-corporate landlord with notice
dormitories, care facilities, nonprofit transitional housing

parsed.doc_summary: San Diego Municipal Code Ch. 9, Art. 8, Div. 7 (§§ 98.0701-98.0710): Residential Tenant Protections ordinance requiring just cause for termination, relocation assistance for no-fault terminations, notices, buyout rules, anti-retaliation and remedies, effective 2023-06-24 and amended 2024-03-28.
